{{Short description|Description of linearly ordered groups}}
{{More footnotes|date=November 2020}}
In [[mathematics]], especially in the area of [[abstract algebra]] dealing with ordered structures on [[abelian group]]s, the '''Hahn embedding theorem''' gives a simple description of all [[linearly ordered group|linearly ordered abelian group]]s. It is named after [[Hans Hahn (mathematician)|Hans Hahn]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=lo.logic - Hahn's Embedding Theorem and the oldest open question in set theory|url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/128935/hahns-embedding-theorem-and-the-oldest-open-question-in-set-theory|access-date=2021-01-28|website=MathOverflow}}</ref>

==Overview==
The theorem states that every linearly ordered abelian group ''G'' can be [[embedding|embedded]] as an ordered [[subgroup]] of the additive group <math>\mathbb{R}^\Omega</math> endowed with a [[lexicographical order]], where <math>\mathbb{R}</math> is the additive group of [[real number]]s (with its standard order), {{math|Ω}} is the set of ''Archimedean [[equivalence class]]es'' of ''G'', and <math>\mathbb{R}^\Omega</math> is the set of all [[function (mathematics)|functions]] from {{math|Ω}} to <math>\mathbb{R}</math> which vanish outside a [[well-ordered set]].
   
Let 0 denote the [[identity element]] of ''G''. For any nonzero element ''g'' of ''G'', exactly one of the elements ''g'' or &minus;''g'' is greater than 0; denote this element by |''g''|.  Two nonzero elements ''g'' and ''h'' of ''G'' are ''Archimedean equivalent'' if there exist [[natural number]]s ''N'' and ''M'' such that ''N''|''g''|&nbsp;>&nbsp;|''h''| and ''M''|''h''|&nbsp;>&nbsp;|''g''|.  Intuitively, this means that neither ''g'' nor ''h'' is "infinitesimal" with respect to the other.  The group ''G'' is [[Archimedean group|Archimedean]] if ''all'' nonzero elements are Archimedean-equivalent.  In this case, {{math|Ω}} is a [[singleton (mathematics)|singleton]], so <math>\mathbb{R}^\Omega</math> is just the group of real numbers.  Then Hahn's Embedding Theorem reduces to [[Otto Hölder|Hölder]]'s theorem, which states that a linearly ordered abelian group is [[Archimedean group|Archimedean]] [[if and only if]] it is a subgroup of the ordered additive group of the real numbers.

{{harvtxt|Gravett|1956}} gives a clear statement and [[mathematical proof|proof]] of the theorem.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gravett |first=K. A. H. |date=1956 |title=ORDERED ABELIAN GROUPS |url=https://academic.oup.com/qjmath/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/qmath/7.1.57 |journal=The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |language=en |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=57–63 |doi=10.1093/qmath/7.1.57 |issn=0033-5606|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  The papers of {{harvtxt|Clifford|1954}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Clifford |first=A. H. |date=December 1954 |title=Note on Hahn's Theorem on Ordered Abelian Groups |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2032549?origin=crossref |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |volume=5 |issue=6 |pages=860 |doi=10.2307/2032549|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and {{harvtxt|Hausner|Wendel|1952}}<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Hausner |first=M. |last2=Wendel |first2=J. G. |date=December 1952 |title=Ordered vector spaces |url=https://www.ams.org/proc/1952-003-06/S0002-9939-1952-0052045-1/ |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=3 |issue=6 |pages=977–982 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1952-0052045-1 |issn=0002-9939}}</ref> together provide another proof.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> See also {{harvtxt|Fuchs|Salce|2001|p=62}}.
